name: Bun quay
summary: Rice-flour noodles with fish, shrimp, squid, herbs, and onion. You mix the sauce from chili, sugar, fish sauce, and citrus. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says the bowl arrived from central Vietnam in 1955 as ground shrimp, was called bún tôm until 1996, and is now served through the day. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Phu Quoc. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says the bowl was brought from central Vietnam in 1955 and was known as bún tôm until 1996.
history: Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says the early bowl was ground shrimp from central Vietnam in 1955. It was called bún tôm until 1996, when the Kiến Xây family tried the island’s seafood and local seasonings. From 1996 to 2012 that family’s kitchen was known across Vietnam for the bowl. The same account says the dish is now cooked in other regions, and that the island is where it started.
culture: The same account calls it a morning dish by tradition, and says it is now served through the day and into the evening. It also says the island has over ten rooms. The day account sends the bowl to Long Beach or Dương Đông.
taste: The sauce is chili, sugar, fish sauce, and citrus. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism calls that mix zest, sweet, salty, and sour.
howToEat: Mix the sauce yourself, then take the noodles, the fish, the shrimp, the squid, the herbs, and the onion.
Order it in the morning on the traditional account, or through the day and into the evening on the same account. Both stay. A price is Check on arrival.
where: Dương Đông, on the street across from the harbour, and along Long Beach. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says the island has over ten rooms. A single door is Check on arrival.
